title: A multi-wave loop has no interface to stop after the current wave; operators SIGINT it from a hand-rolled watcher
summary: Console PRs must merge only between waves, so the operator needs the running loop to stop cleanly at the next wave boundary. `.evolve/loop-stop` brakes only a chained loop (`--until-inbox-empty`) at a batch boundary; a `--max-cycles N` run spanning several waves has no brake, so the console tailed the log for the wave-close line and sent SIGINT to the exact pid (a session script). The interim is one wave per run (`--max-cycles` = fleet width). Found 2026-09-28 (gap G3).
fix: Honor the existing brake at wave boundaries too: the multi-wave window checks paths.LoopStopFile before launching the next wave and ends the run with stop_reason `brake` (no new wave, the finished wave sealed). One brake file for both boundaries, no new flag. Document `touch .evolve/loop-stop` as the stop-after-this-wave control in runtime-reference.md.
acceptance: A multi-wave run with .evolve/loop-stop present ends after the running wave with stop_reason brake, launching no further wave (red today: it launches the next wave)
A chained run still stops at its batch boundary
runtime-reference.md names the brake as the stop-after-this-wave control
source: console, 2026-09-28, interface-discipline inventory at the wave-26 boundary (gap G3)
consumed_by: console landing fix/loop-controls (2026-09-29): BUILT. prepareIteration honours the existing brake (loopchain.BrakeEngaged) at every iteration's start, the first included, before the probes and any refresh; the run ends with stop_reason loop_operator_brake after the ordinary closeout (finalize, batch-end sweep, dossiers published on exit). A chained run stops the batch at its wave boundary and the chain at its batch boundary. New verb `evolve loop-stop` engages the brake (timestamp line) and `evolve loop-stop --release` removes it; runtime-reference.md's wave-boundary protocol stops with it and launches after the release.
